target_customer: Smallholder farmers in Africa buying crop insurance by mobile money, and reinsurers and investors who take the risk
problem: Smallholder farmers cannot get affordable insurance against drought. WorldCover sold rainfall based parametric cover and passed risk to global reinsurers.
business_model: Parametric micro crop insurance sold through mobile channels with premiums shared with reinsurers

founders.name: Christopher Sheehan
founders.background_notes: YC page and TechCrunch 2019 name him co-founder and CEO. Background not found in an opened source.

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining satellite rainfall data, USSD mobile sales and mobile money payouts, plus reinsurance structuring, is standard engineering with hard regulatory and risk parts.

defensibility.rationale: Licensed broker status in Ghana, Kenya and Uganda and reinsurer relationships such as Swiss Re and Nephila took time to build, though others sold index insurance.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquirer found. Catalyst Fund lists WorldCover as no longer operating.

market_need_then: The company's pitch said over 70 percent of the 2.5 billion people at the base of the pyramid rely on agriculture and lack disaster cover. By May 2019 it had served over 30,000 farmers in Ghana, Uganda and Kenya.

branding.domain_note: Domain not verified; www.worldcover.org did not resolve in this session.

brand_strength.rationale: Press covered the funding rounds and product, but nothing shows the brand itself drove growth.

pivots.from: Peer-to-peer investment platform funding global insurance
pivots.to: Parametric micro crop insurance for African smallholders sold via mobile
pivots.why: not stated; compare the YC description with the 2019 TechCrunch product description

outcome_analysis: WorldCover moved from a peer-to-peer insurance funding idea in YC W16 to selling parametric crop insurance in Ghana, Uganda and Kenya, reaching over 30,000 farmers and raising a 6 million USD Series A in May 2019 led by MS&AD Ventures. The Catalyst Fund page now lists it as no longer operating, but no source gives the date or cause, so the cause is not public and failure factors stay empty.
notes: The 2016 seed (amount unknown) rests on CB Insights alone and the 50K Catalyst Fund grant on village.do alone; Bouncewatch lists further undisclosed rounds in 2017 and January 2018, not recorded. Total raised is commonly cited as about 6.1M USD, so the Series A accounts for nearly all of it. A profile aggregator names Shiliang Tang as a co-founder; unverified and not recorded. TechCrunch 2019 names Pula and Mobbisurance as other agricultural insurance startups, but that source is three years after the batch so the competitor list is empty. YC still describes the older peer-to-peer concept. The company website could not be fetched.
